title: Specialized federal common law
summary: Specialized federal common law consists of judicially developed federal rules supported by particular federal interests or authority, rather than a general power arising from federal jurisdiction.
notes: A federal connection alone does not justify replacing all state law. The readings emphasize restrictions on judicial lawmaking and differences among the recognized settings.

sections.Meaning: Specialized federal common law consists of judicially developed federal rules supported by particular federal interests or authority, rather than a general power arising from federal jurisdiction.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the federal interest and the need for displacement of state law. Then ask whether federal law should supply a distinct rule or borrow state law. Compare the government payment instrument in Clearfield with the procurement conflict and specific conditions in Boyle.
